title: vessel
content_html:
vessel

In little clear vessel, the vessel is empty and open and somehow contains a couple’s love. Memory loss vessels and the body made for Doll give other forms to the idea of holding something invisible. What does a container allow its contents to do? It might preserve them, carry them somewhere else or give shape to something we could scarcely describe. Giving an invisible thing a place to live also gives us a place to look if it escapes. little clear vessel · Memory loss vessels I

Reading note. Alchemy, Jung and Daoism. Jung discusses the hermetic vessel as part of the alchemical work. Chapter 11 of the Daodejing attends to the empty space that makes a vessel useful. Both images meet in little clear vessel. What can happen because something is held inside, and what can happen because space is kept available? Psychology and Alchemy, §338 · Daodejing, 11
